notes.title: Northern Regime Pre-Alpha 3.0.5
notes.content:
[h1] INTRODUCTION [/h1]

Hey, everyone! I hope you are all enjoying yourselves this weekend. We have been working really hard on the progression of Northern Regime, but unfortunately, my computer has been overheating and crashing constantly. It's fixed now, but I did miss quite a bit of work this week. 

Next week we'll be right back on our usual hardworking schedule.


[h1] FARMING [/h1]

This is the very first iteration on farming in Northern Regime. Building and construction are something we want focused on mostly, especially giving the players a choice to steal and kill or not to and just survive the wild.

This first iteration only includes one single type of crop and seed; potatoes. Before I continue to start adding more and more types of crops I'm going to do a little research on agriculture to better understand how it all works. 

To farm is pretty simple right now, we plan to make it more and more complex requiring watering, raking, and trimming. Currently, you just need to have the seed in your inventory, go into building mode, select the potato, and finally place the flower bed anywhere you want. I like the flower beds they're actually pretty decorative, you can place them inside of your house if you want to. Once the potato plant is placed it will take around 5 minutes to fully grow to the point of where you can harvest them. 

It's very basic but this is the first iteration and I think it is pretty good for now.

[h1] ADDITIONS [/h1]

[list]
[*][b] New Railing Block [/b]
We have added a cool, decorative wooden railing to the crafting and building menu. It doesn't hold purpose for defense or anything other than looks. Using this railing block you can now create a pretty interesting porch for your cabin. Later on, this railing will serve as a minor defense against enemies. 

[*][b] Advancement On Butchering [/b]
Butchering was very basic prior. You would just click the dead deer body from anywhere on the map. It's changed now, it may not be as advanced as it should be but we will continue to improve on it. To skin a deer you have to go up to its body and wield your hatchet. You then can stab the deer once, blood will appear on your screen and you will gain the meat.

[*][b] Item Slot Indicator [/b] 
In-game there wasn't an indication to let players know which weapon they were holding if they were not directly looking at their player's hand. When you switch weapons now, you will see a little icon in the top left of your screen showing you what you are holding. This should help fix some old confusion around equipping items. 
[/list]

[h1] SMALL FIXES OR ADDITIONS [/h1]

[list]
[*] Fixed most trees and tree colliders. Some are still buggy and will need to be fixed.

[*] Fixed a small crafting menu bug; items were not showing up first time clicked.

[*] Changed Iron Ore Model. 

[*] Players now start with food and a hatchet.

[*] Tweaked survival setting again.

[*] Fixed animal colliders. Players were able to ride deer which didn't seem quite right.
[/list]
[h1] OUTRO [/h1]

Thank you, everyone. Sorry, this update wasn't as big as it should have been. My computer is fixed now so I am ready to work hard these next two weeks to get a massive and awesome update for you all. The next update will come two Fridays after this. 

If you have any questions or find bugs in this new update, please feel free to let me know!

notes.title: Northern Regime Hot Fix 4
notes.content:
[h1] INTRODUCTION [/h1]

Hey, everyone! So for today's hotfix, we've added a few items, fixed some bugs, and confusion. We've changed some crafting methods and requirements for different items. Let's go through it!


[h1] ADDITIONS [/h1]

[list]
[*] We have added a [b]workbench[/b] to Northern Regime. This item will now show up in your crafting menu and building menu. You can only place it outside on the terrain. We'll have different workbenches that will be placed inside your structure. Some items will require you to be near a crafting bench. Here is a small list; Bullets, pistol, rifle, wall, roof, platform, stairs, pliers, weapon repairs for all items including pickaxe, pistol, rifle, and hatchet. So, basically, every large item requires a crafting bench now.

[*] [b]Weapon health and repairs[/b]. Previously the only items that needed repairs were your pistol and rifle. We have added repairs to your pickaxe and hatchet now. All repairs take pretty much the same amount of resources. The damage rate on your pickaxe and hatchet is not bad. Each strike with a pickaxe deletes -2 health and a hatchet is -3. Your weapons do not deplete in health while attacking deer or soldiers. 

[*][b] Stones [/b] We added stones to the crafting and inventory system yesterday but now they are an item you can find. Before in-game there were the stones/rocks on the ground you could not pick up and that confused players, luckily now, you can pick them up. Each stone give +1 stone to your inventory. 

[*][b] Hunger Increasing Health [/b] If your hunger is now over 70 percent it will slowly increase your character's health over time. It is not the quickest thing as a bandage would still be a more realistic approach, but if you aren't in combat and just wondering I guess there wouldn't be a reason to waste a bandage.

[*][b] Mouse Sensitivity Slider[/b] We have added a slider to adjust your sensitivity in-game. It is located in your setting page. Please note that you most likely need to go change it right away! If you hop in now it will most likely be set to 0 because the number doesn't exist in your save. So just go edit it and save your game and you won't any longer have that problem. The smallest sensitivity is 0 and the highest is 150. If 150 is still too small for you, we can raise the cap.

[*][b] In-Game Guide Book[/b] We have added a guide book for in-game use that uses illustrations to explain how to do specific things. I'd recommend you check it out I think it's pretty cool. Right now there are only four different pages explaining the basics, but we are going to be expanding on it every single day until we have covered everything. I hope even right now it will clear up a lot of the confusion.

[*][b] Trading Is In[/b] We have added trading. You just need to walk up to a camp and press tab near a soldier. A little trading menu will come up on your right. Right now you can only buy things from soldiers they won't sell you anything. This is the way it will be until we add friendly camps, with union soldiers. You can expect this with-in the next week or so.
[/list]
[h1] SMALL TWEAKS[/h1]
We've made a couple small tweaks. I can't for the life of me remember them all but here are a few.
[list]
[*] Changes some of the levels for being able to craft a pistol and a rifle.
[*] Hunger and Temp do not go down as fast anymore
[*] Some food now increases hunger bar more.
[*] [b] Optimization Boost [/b] When we added the new pickup system there was a lot of lag that came with it. We realized our code was actually pretty sloppy and misdirected. We have since cleaned it up and increased the average framerate by 15-20. 


[/list]
[h1] OUTRO + QUICK QUESTION[/h1]
Once again, everyone, these changes would not have been made if it weren't for all of your suggestions and criticism so thank you so much and keep it coming!

Once question I have is; are you guys enjoying the frequency of these updates and hotfixes or would you rather they come out once a week or longer?

Thanks!

notes.title: Northern Regime Pre-Alpha 3.0.2
notes.content:
[h1] INTRODUCTION [/h1]

Hey, everyone!
 Today I am calling this new build an update because it does change the game in a semi-major way. Because it isn't our normal or planned update, which should be every two weeks I am calling it 3.0.2 instead of what it would be; 3.1.0.

[b][i] BUILD IS LIVE [/i][/b]

[h1] CHANGES [/h1]
[list]
[*][b] Resource Gathering [/b]

 We have changed the gathering of ores and other items. Some items still use the old system and will remain that way. Previously we used a timer system, you would click the ore, the timer would start, then at the end of the timer the object would disappear and you would receive the items. The changed version: Now you need to wield your pickaxe or hatchet depending on the mineral you are wanting to mine. You need to be with-in a short distance of the object, you then look at that object, click it and an animation will play of your character smashing the object. All items take the same amount of hits right now; 4. We're going to be changing that shortly.

[*][b] Destroying Doors[/b]

 If you haven't heard, we changed some camps to cabins. Before you had to shoot down the door in order to get through. This has been changed. Although it's been changed you can still shoot the door down. Now you can smash the door down with a hatchet or pickaxe. 
[/list]
[*] [b]Notice [/b]

Please notice; because you need a pickaxe to mine iron and because you need iron to make a pickaxe it doesn't "compute" to make a pickaxe you'll now need stone. Stone is a material we have yet to add, for now when you log in you will automatically receive 25 stone, 7 more than what is needed. Pickaxe will not require repairs until we can add stone. 

The new animation for mining is currently a placeholder and will be changed until we can get an improved version.

Some audio used for the new improvements are also placeholders that will be improved in some upcoming hotfixes.

[h1] ADDITIONS 

[/h1]
[list]


[*][b] Melee Weapons [/b] 

We have finally added melee weapons to Northern Regime.

[i] Please notice I've only spent 8 hours on this system as I just began this morning, just saying this as it may be a little buggy for the start. Expect hot patches throughout today and tomorrow for this addition. [/i] 

You can now use a hatchet or pickaxe to kill soldiers and deer. We have yet to set it for bears, it's not urgent because we're not sure if it would even be possible to kill a bear that close. Enemies take about two hits. The reason we made it so low is because of that fact you have to get so close to the enemy just to be able to kill them. Deer currently take 5 hits.

[*][b] Sneaking [/b]

Because we now have melee weapons the sneaking in Northern Regime will begin to expand. Enemies have only ever attacked if you were in their vision of sight which is about 90-120 degrees or so. Sneaking wasn't practical because they do attack if you fire off a shot. Now you should be able to get up behind someone and kill them without others knowing. Camps are quite small right now and the enemies are near each other, sneaking still isn't the most practical option because of that. We will begin to create larger camps that are more spread out. In addition, enemies will start patrolling. < This is not in currently but expect it sometime soon. We still need to add crouching to make these scenarios more realistic. 
[/list]

[h1] NEXT HOT PATCHES [/h1]

[i] Just want to let you all know what I'll be adding next as a hot patch. Because we have been getting so many suggestions and bug reports the next large update may not come exactly on time or contain what was originally planned [/i]

[list] 
[*][b] In-game Instructions Book[/b]
We realize, from you guys ([i] Thanks again for all of the constructive critisim[/i]) That having the instructions on a web page is not the most optimal system. We also have noticed and heard from you all, that the instructions are outdated and not in-depth enough. 

We will be changing to an in-game booklet that will have many pages on every single item or system in the game. To better explain each system we will be using text and images/illustrations to define how they work. This is what I will be working on now and for the next 10 or so hours. I'm hoping this system will stop any confusion you have been experiencing.

[*][b] Sticks & Stones Confusion [/b]
Because some sticks in-game are there just for decoration and others to be interacted with, we realize how users are finding this confusing for their first time. We are going to work on a different terrain detail that will stop this confusion from happening again.

[*][b] Minor Additions [/b]

[i] We may also be adding a map. It will take a while to brainstorm how it should work and then if we come up with a solid system we will begin adding it.

We are also going to tweak hunger. When you hunger bar is high it will slowly increase health over time.
[/i]

[i] Hunger & Temp have been changed to decrease a little slower than before [/i] 

[i] A known bug that will need to be fixed is our experience and levels. For some reason they are not updating(experience) until you level up. It will be fixed in the next hot patch! [/i]

[/list]

[h1] OUTRO [/h1]

Thank you, everyone. I hope you enjoy. If anyone has issues with the new update please email me or post in the forums and I will respond right away. If you have any suggestions or criticism I would love to hear it!

See you all soon!

notes.title: Northern Regime Hot Fix 3
notes.content:
Hey, everyone. This is a super small hotfix/update but I think it's pretty cool and should add a little more excitement or incentive to attack camps.

We swapped a few camp style outposts for confederate cabins. The only way to get into a cabin is to actually shoot the door down. To knock a door down it should take anywhere from 3-4 shots total. 

These cabins have a cool design with beds, tables, chairs, and a fireplace. They also now have a ton more loot and food. What we are going to be doing is giving each base cabin a rating out of ten. one out of ten would be the lowest difficulty and ten would be the highest. The cabins will also get more complicated and larger depending on the difficulty. 

This hotfix also includes a small optimization boost. We took most and every static detail in Northern Regime and combined it into one single mesh. This, in theory, should reduce draw calls which in most cases is the result of lag or poor performance aside from a lot of cases where it could be poor programming. 

Once we have added a lot of confederate bases we will be taking away their respawn. Once you destroy a base the enemies will not come back and neither their items, however, the cabins will still be there but they will no longer have doors. 

I'll be uploading another hotfix in the next few hours with some tweaks based on what everyone has been saying. We've received some complaints that the hunger and temperature are going down too quickly. We are going to alter it a little, but in the upcoming days, we are going to add difficulty levels.

This will be the last hotfix post because we need to start working on the next big update we won't be able to upload hotfix builds because the world won't be stable. 

The next update is going to be on building and Construction. We'll hopefully be adding the following to the crafting menu; Torches, crafting table, fireplace, table, doors, door frames, a smelter for smelting minerals, a stove, and possibly a few others. 

Thanks for the support everyone. Any questions, I'd love to answer them!

notes.title: Northern Regime Pre-Alpha 2.9.0
notes.content:
[h1] Northern Regime's Launch Information. [/h1]

[b] Launch Date, Price, & Times.[/b]
[list]
[*]Northern Regime is launching in just under 1 day, now. (Friday 17th)
[*]Our launch price will be 10.99 USD | 10.99 Euro | 11.99 CAD | 7.99 GBP | 259 Russian Rubles with a discount percentage of 10%.
[*]Launch hour: 1:00 pm Pacific Time - 4:00 pm Eastern Standard - 2200  central European time
[/list]
[b] How Updates & Patches Will Work [/b]
[list]
[*] Updates will come out every third Friday starting on launch day which will be a Friday. 
[*] The first update will come out the second Friday after launch, being 2 weeks rather than three.
[*] Patches and bug repairs will come out every second day depending on how severe they are. (We are not sure if updates will remove building we will update you on that soon)
[*] All in-game items will be saved when you update Northern Regime so you don't have to worry about starting over again.
[*] This will be the last update before Northern Regime's early access launch: Northern Regime Pre-Alpha 3.0
[*] Update intervals will work like this; A large update will be a whole 0.1.0, and small updates or large patches will be 0.0.5.
[/list]

[h1] Northern Regime: 2.9.0. [/h1]

[b] What We've Added or Improved. [/b]
[list]
[*] [b]Modular Building & Saving.[/b] Modular building right now only includes a bed, walls, foundations, and stairs. We are going to expand adding many more items, firstly roofs, doors, and windowed walls. 
[*] [b]Hostile Bears[/b] We've added bears that will attack if in a certain radius. They also have health bars that appear above their heads. Bears will also make a noise if in a certain radius.
[*][b] Gun Reticle [/b] We have added a new dynamic weapon reticle. This reticle will sway as you move your mouse. This makes it more realistic as if you would need time to adjust to your target. The reticle will now also flash red if you hit an enemy. Before there was not such indication of hitting a target.
[*][b] Dawn - Dusk Cycle[/b] This was more a personal decision than anything else. I do not like playing video games in the dark. So our new cycle will go from morning then a somewhat dark pre-night(Dusk) then it will cycle backward to the morning. We will see the response, and if needed, switch to a full day and night cycle.
[*][b] Weapon Switching[/b] Small but a great change. To switch between your items you will now use the scroll wheel rather than your number keys. We did this because it feels much better, but it will also help free up the key inputs for building parts.
[*][b] Player Damage [/b] We have changed from the dynamic damage system, we didn't feel it was ready, also thinking it was too complicated and annoying to play a part of the in-game experience. We have switched to a basic bandaging system to heal yourself. You need to craft bandages so it will still be dynamic. 
[*][b] Sounds & Music [/b]We have worked on the in-game sound effects, they will still need additional work as we are not totally happy with them just yet. The rifle shot has been enhanced and deepened. Previously the musket shot felt a little weak and unrealistic. The new sound now has some base and depth to it. An action instrumental song has been added thanks to our composer, Seth. This track will play while engaging in gun fights or being attacked. Increases immersion. 
[*][b]Indicators[/b] Some really cool indicators will now pop up to help you while playing Northern Regime. I play NR quite a bit so I know how everything works, but I realized a lot of people won't understand. I've taken some steps to helping those players out. If your gun is broken and needs repairs a pop-up will tell you that. The same goes for when you run out of ammo or dismantle an object. We will continue to add more!
[*][b] Dismantling Constructed Items[/b] Building may be buggy in the start. There is still lots of work to be done, that being said we want the player to be able to dismantle and object like a wall and actually get that piece back in their inventory. We think this will be fair in the start. 
[*][b]Enemy Camp Changes[/b] We have taken a few steps to increase the liveliness of enemy camps. Ai has not been our main focus recently. Later we will have camp members wandering, gathering, and constructing. For now, we have just given enemies more animations. Before they just stood there and watched you. Now, enemies may be sitting, leaning, or sleeping.
[/list]

[h1] See You All On Day One![/h1]

notes.title: Northern Regime Pre-Alpha 2.8.1
notes.content:
[h1] Player Skills Tree [/h1]
Today we are introducing the "Player Skills Tree" this tree will give you certain upgrades and abilities as you level up in-game. Using the skill tree will be crucial to in-game progression.
[list]
    [*] Bush Craft: Increases wood yield by over 50 percent. 
    [*] Miner: Increases Ore yields by 50 percent.
    [*] Rifle Expert: Increases bullet damage by 75 percent making all enemies a one shot kill.
[*] Survivor: Hunger and Warmth decrease at a much slower rate. Eating does 2x more. 
[*] Veteran: Decreases enemy bullet damage by over 50 percent.
[/list]

The Skill Tree creates a new dynamic to Northern Regime. It will be up to you to decide whether to chose bushcraft or Miner first. It may take trial and error figuring out what crafting recipes take what materials and what you need to craft first in order to survive. 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25855610/da16175e302ae1081c7c3b15e8a1134ce1b954ce.png[/img]

[h1] Player Anatomy Analysis(Injury System) [/h1]

We have not worked out the system completely but we are very excited about it. Healing will no longer be simple in Northern Regime. 
[b] How It Works [/b]
Depending on where you get shot it will show you specifically on the anatomy analysis chart. If you get shot in the chest it will tell you what you need to craft to survive and heal your injury. Each part of your body will require a different medical kit. Some kits will be very rare and difficult to craft. This will make Northern Regime even more challenging! 

[img]http://cdn.akamai.steamstatic.com/steamcommunity/public/images/clans/25855610/3fb8b8d168bcafd3cc9d1dcae841e9779bbaf316.png[/img]

[h1] Localization [/h1]
Gladly Nothern Regime has been translated to Russian, French, and German. We will continue to expand and hopefully, have 12-15 total languages upon full release! Thanks, everyone!

notes.title: New Building & Crafting Systems
notes.content:
[h1] Building [/h1]

Building in Northern Regime will be a little different than most survival games. Instead of building randomly with blocks, you will have the option to build on to a pre-existing foundation once you have found the corresponding blueprints which are randomly generated in chests.

[b] Building Items [/b]
[list]
    [*] House Walls
    [*] An old style bed 
[b] Bed's [/b] [i] If you do not have a bed and die in Northern Regime, your save file will be deleted forcing you to start over. If you do have a bed your file will save, as well, you will have the option to press "H" and teleport back to your home.
    [*] Add art like paintings or deer heads
    [*] Add a carpet or rug
    [*] Add torches for light
    [*] Sawmill to collect wood
  [i] And plenty more to come. Let us know if you like this system style.[/i]
[/list]

[h1] What Else? [/h1]

We plan to add Head Hunters to Northern Regime after you have created your first home. They have seen you start to progress and become stronger so they have developed jealousy. They will spawn randomly and try to attack you. 

This will hopefully create an interesting dynamic and a feeling of uneasiness. Will will hopefully throw in some traps and home defense. Maybe also the ability for bandits to steal or harm your home. 

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=7QJ597BiY_E&feature=youtu.be&ab_channel=NorthernRegime

[h1] New Crafting System & UI [/h1]

Our crafting has changed for the better. It is more organized and stylized more efficiently. Crafting items will show up in a list form. You will click the item you want to craft and it will show up in a little crafting box. This crafting box will display the items you need and the quantity it takes to create them. When ready there is now a big button saying "Craft" you can click it and a timer will begin to progress until complete.

[h1] Development Vlog [/h1]

Be sure to check out our most recent development vlog. It shows some of the stuff we added to Pre-Alpha 2.8.

https://www.youtube.com/watch?v=T1BptIwJ2Y8&ab_channel=NorthernRegime

notes.title: Update Pre-Alpha 2.8.0
notes.content:
[h1] Introduction [/h1] 

Since Northern Regime releases into [b]Early Access in just 30 days[/b] we have been working as hard as we can! I'm still a little sick so I haven't been able to make a development vlog, but I hope to make one soon.

This will most likely be the biggest update yet. We have been working and adding plenty of mechanics, systems, new items, new crafting recipes, and much more. We'll go over as many as we can remember in this update. However, this update will be the last of which we go into detail about items and new mechanics as we want some what of a mystery for when you first play Northern Regime.

[h1] New Additions [/h1]

[list]
[h1] Food [/h1]
    [*] New foods that can be found at camps and throughout hidden areas; Chocolate bars, beans, and beef jerky.
[h1] Terrain Details[/h1]
    [*]Added new trees and bushes. 
    [*]Added large mountainscapes in the distance.
[*] Added a lot of small terrain details; rocks, sticks, tree branches, leafs.
[b][i] All of these detail additions really help make the world feel dense and mysterious. It's a small addition but makes the biggest difference.[/i] [/b]
[h1] Textures & Models [/h1]
[*] Added higher quality textures for the terrain and the character model.
[*] Added a much more realistic snowfall that actually appears on the grand near you for a particular duration.
[*] Added a super high-quality backpack model for the character. We decided to spend the money on contracting a very expensive artist for this, because the back of the character is something you will be seeing a lot of. It's important to have something visually stunning to look at. 
[h1] Sound & Audio[/h1]
[*] We have been working on our custom sound effects. We have commissioned a small studio to create these. It's been going well, we are happy to have our own unique sounds.
[*] Our sound composer has been working super hard producing plenty of music for our soundtrack. We currently only have 3 songs in the soundtrack but we hope for around 12 or so by lunch. The music is really great and works well to set the in-game atmosphere.
[h1] Crafting & Inventory[/h1]
[*] We have spent an immense time on the crafting and inventory ui/mechanics. We have re-worked the ui for the inventory and the crafting menu. The crafting menu now has better icon images down by a professional. The inventory now has photo-realistic icons that make gathering items feel more satisfying. We haven't just been working on the visuals, we have also been working quite hard on adding awesome new items and crafting recipes. The most notable item we added was a rabbit snare. You'll be able to place as many as you want and they'll naturally trap animals you'll be able to cook then eat.
[h1] Site & Steam [/h1]
[*] If you haven't noticed, we launched a new trailer on our Steam page, also adding new screenshots. We'll most likely continue adding new images and videos as we get closer to launch because the game is changing so much in visual and just getting better generally. Our website has also been re-worked completely. We suggest you check it out pretty soon here we'll have a tutorial page for new players.
[h1] Inventory & Weapons [/h1]
[*] We want Northern Regime to be a pretty tough game. We have decided to add item health to tools, weapons, and traps. Previously you could use your gun or pickaxe for as long as you wanted to. Now they actually have health and durability. When a weapon loses all health it automatically is destroyed. In the future, we would like to make the particular tool you are using become less useful as loses durability. We also need to add toolkits. We have added a pickaxe and a hatchet; the pickaxe helps you mine faster, and the hatchet increases your yield. 
[h1] Combat [/h1]
[*] Comabt is definitely getting better and more fun. We have added a weapon level system into Northern Regime. When you start out it is going to take you a while to kill an enemy(3-4 shots total) This is going to force the player to level up before taking on larger camps. There are 3 levels max, the 3rd level being a one shot kill. To level up you will need to craft rifle upgrades.
[h1] Visuals [/h1]
[*] Visuals are important to us(obviously not more important than gameplay). So we have been working a lot on different effects for the camera. The most recent is a radial blur. It's again a pretty small addition but it really does affect immersion. When scoped out it's pretty minor just around the edges, but when you zoom in it spreads quite far into the center making it feel like your character is actually focusing in on what you are aiming at. It makes combat really awesome and interesting.
[/list]

[h1] Launch Plan [/h1]

So the early access launch date is final.([i]Hopefully lol[/i]). We will be releasing Northern Regime's alpha on February 17th at 1:00 pm Pacific Time. Most places in America that will be around 4:00 pm. 

So a question most of you are probably wondering is "When will updates/patches come out?" The answer is [b] Every second Saturday[/b]
So basically every 2 weeks. We would like to do it every week, which we originally planned for, but I think it would be best for everybody if we waited two weeks instead. We will be able to add more items, mechanics, systems, etc and also be able to focus more on bugs and errors you may experience.

We hope that everybody loves the game and it is everything you anticipated. I'll talk to you all soon!

[*] Added a lot of small terrain details; rocks, sticks, tree branches, leafs.
[b][i] All of these detail additions really help make the world feel dense and mysterious. It's a small addition but makes the biggest difference.[/i] [/b]
[h1] Textures & Models [/h1]
[*] Added higher quality textures for the terrain and the character model.
[*] Added a much more realistic snowfall that actually appears on the grand near you for a particular duration.
[*] Added a super high-quality backpack model for the character. We decided to spend the money on contracting a very expensive artist for this, because the back of the character is something you will be seeing a lot of. It's important to have something visually stunning to look at. 
[h1] Sound & Audio[/h1]
[*] We have been working on our custom sound effects. We have commissioned a small studio to create these. It's been going well, we are happy to have our own unique sounds.
[*] Our sound composer has been working super hard producing plenty of music for our soundtrack. We currently only have 3 songs in the soundtrack but we hope for around 12 or so by lunch. The music is really great and works well to set the in-game atmosphere.
[h1] Crafting & Inventory[/h1]
[*] We have spent an immense time on the crafting and inventory ui/mechanics. We have re-worked the ui for the inventory and the crafting menu. The crafting menu now has better icon images down by a professional. The inventory now has photo-realistic icons that make gathering items feel more satisfying. We haven't just been working on the visuals, we have also been working quite hard on adding awesome new items and crafting recipes. The most notable item we added was a rabbit snare. You'll be able to place as many as you want and they'll naturally trap animals you'll be able to cook then eat.
[h1] Site & Steam [/h1]
[*] If you haven't noticed, we launched a new trailer on our Steam page, also adding new screenshots. We'll most likely continue adding new images and videos as we get closer to launch because the game is changing so much in visual and just getting better generally. Our website has also been re-worked completely. We suggest you check it out pretty soon here we'll have a tutorial page for new players.
[h1] Inventory & Weapons [/h1]
[*] We want Northern Regime to be a pretty tough game. We have decided to add item health to tools, weapons, and traps. Previously you could use your gun or pickaxe for as long as you wanted to. Now they actually have health and durability. When a weapon loses all health it automatically is destroyed. In the future, we would like to make the particular tool you are using become less useful as loses durability. We also need to add toolkits. We have added a pickaxe and a hatchet; the pickaxe helps you mine faster, and the hatchet increases your yield. 
[h1] Combat [/h1]
[*] Comabt is definitely getting better and more fun. We have added a weapon level system into Northern Regime. When you start out it is going to take you a while to kill an enemy(3-4 shots total) This is going to force the player to level up before taking on larger camps. There are 3 levels max, the 3rd level being a one shot kill. To level up you will need to craft rifle upgrades.
[h1] Visuals [/h1]
[*] Visuals are important to us(obviously not more important than gameplay). So we have been working a lot on different effects for the camera. The most recent is a radial blur. It's again a pretty small addition but it really does affect immersion. When scoped out it's pretty minor just around the edges, but when you zoom in it spreads quite far into the center making it feel like your character is actually focusing in on what you are aiming at. It makes combat really awesome and interesting.
[/list]

[h1] Launch Plan [/h1]

So the early access launch date is final.([i]Hopefully lol[/i]). We will be releasing Northern Regime's alpha on February 17th at 1:00 pm Pacific Time. Most places in America that will be around 4:00 pm. 

So a question most of you are probably wondering is "When will updates/patches come out?" The answer is [b] Every second Saturday[/b]
So basically every 2 weeks. We would like to do it every week, which we originally planned for, but I think it would be best for everybody if we waited two weeks instead. We will be able to add more items, mechanics, systems, etc and also be able to focus more on bugs and errors you may experience.

We hope that everybody loves the game and it is everything you anticipated. I'll talk to you all soon!

notes.title: Pre-Alpha 2.7.0
notes.content:
[h1] Introduction.[/h1]

Hey, everyone! Sorry for the lack of updates recently. I've been feeling pretty under the weather. I'm doing a lot better now and that means back to work. 

Because I've been sick I haven't been able to get much work done so there has been a lack of progression in Northern Regime.

    [*] 7 different enemy fortress' to attack and raid. 7 may sound like a small number but these camps are actually quite large and are re-raidable. We are going for a somewhat "Borderlands" style farming system when it comes to enemies. 
[*] over 10 different materials used to gather, to craft, or to heal.
[*] Random building to search and to loot.
[*] Basic clue based story line. The story line is not complete, but if you are smart and tedious enough, you may be able to figure it out.
[*] Of course, there is so much more but here his a minor list to give an idea of what Northern Regime has to offer.

[b] Early Access games are often buggy and unfinished, we understand that. We can't promise a polished finish game because that's not what it will be on the 17th. If you are looking for a complete game, we ask you to hold off buying Northern Regime. Although we say that, Northern Regime right now is still a fun and great experience to play. [/b]

[/list]

[h1] Goals For EA [/h1]

It is in the game but because it is such a difficult component to master it is not working perfectly in many ways. We are going to do our best to finish it off. We are going to decide which components or functions are priority one.
    [*] Character trading: Pretty close with character interaction, character trading will be pretty important to find new items, or sell items to acquire the things you need. This is one of the most complicated functions.
    [*] Position Location System: Because everything in the world respawns back in when you do, we need to figure out the best spawning system that will go arm and arm with that. If you spawn where you quit the game you'll be able to mine the materials you just mined, which seems too easy. We are thinking of a random spawn with in a certain radius. 

[b] There are quite a few other small things we plan to get done before release, we promise to keep you all updated as we progress. You can follow me on twitter for continous updates.[/b]

[/list]

[h1] Conclusion [/h1]

Thank you all so much for the amazing support. It means the world to me knowing there are people out there excited for something that I created, and spent so much work on. I can't wait to include you all into the development once we launch. I hope we have a great devoted community. I'll see you all soon!

notes.title: First Implementation Of Sneaking & Fortress'
notes.content:
[h1] Sneaking Now & Future Improvements [/h1]

We finally have started working on sneaking. Sneaking is something we have wanted for quite a while, but we really didn't know how we were going to put it in Northern Regime. Since there is reputation in the game and how some  enemies won't attack unless you have poor reputation or if you have a weapon out. 
[b]
Here are the basics of the sneaking system.
[/b]
[list]
    [*]Enemies have a field of vision of 90 degrees on the Y and X axis. If you enter that area and you are near enough they will notice you and begin watching. If your reputation is poor or if you have a weapon out they will begin attacking.
    [*]If one enemy of the specific camp you are near attacks you, he will also let his fellow camp members know, and they will all start attacking
    [*] We have introduced silenced weapons, such as old rifles and some pistols. Because we don't have melee weapons sneaking wouldn't make sense otherwise, unless you were just attempting to steal resources. We don't have silenced rifles clips yet so we just turned down the rifle volume and increased the pitch to sound less threatening.
[/list]

[b] Some things we want to add to make the experience more realistic and challenging [/b]

[list]
    [*] Enemies triggered by noise, such as opening chests, walking to close, or mining materials nearby. We would also like to take in account the speed and sound of wind to diffuse certain situations. 
    [*] Enemies as of now do not wander or patrol their area. This would help make sneaking into camps harder, more strategic, and an increase in realism. 
    [*] There is definitely a lot we can do with this new implementation, so if you have any ideas please feel free to comment on this post!
[/list]

[h1] Enemy Fortress' [/h1]

Enemy camps haven't been what we originally imagined them as. We didn't notice it either. Camps have consisted of around 4 tents, a couple resources, and 3-4 enemies total. That was really it. It wasn't immersive, exciting, fun, or realistic. It just didn't seem right. Here are some things we added to make it a lot better.


[list]
    [*]Full-scale fencing or some fencing to guard the perimeter. 
    [*]Guard towers to give enemies increased visual distance, as well as an easy identifier for the player notice camps before it's too late.
    [*]Loot chests you can take after defeating the camp unless you sneak passed the soldiers. These chests contain mostly all resources including ammo.
[*] Created blueprints for camps the player can trade resources to get, from other camps or tribes. This will make it easier to deceive your target or to sneak in more efficiently. 
[*] The layout is larger in general and more spread out to a bigger degree. Camps before were very compressed, it made it feel far too fake. 
[*] We have added much more foliage, rocks, and trees. This makes the camp dense and harder to identify. It also makes gun fights more challenging as it is harder to spot the area where an enemy may be attacking from.
[/list]

[b] This are some basic additions that do really make it a better and challenging. We are going to continue adding to this. We want raiding to be a big part of gameplay, and as now it is still now where we want it to be.


Things we would like to add[/b]

[list]
    [*]More structures like tree blinds the enemies can hide in and surprise the player.
    [*]Enemy traps like holes in the ground near entrances that the player could fall in.
    [*]Possible camp allies that would come to their aid if in serious trouble. 
[*] Camp scouts. They would patrol larger areas around the camps radious to be on the look out for possible threats. They would alert the camp if you were to be spotted. 
[*] Camp bounty hunters. These men would be paid to hunt you down after you have attacked their camp, poor reputation or not. 
[/list]

notes.title: Pre-Alpha 2.0.65
notes.content:
[h1] Progress Introduction	[/h1]

Hey, everyone. It's been a while since the last update a result of being busy. I thought I'd update everyone on the progress we have made since, and where development is heading. We'll also talk a little on the release date.

[h1] System and Mechanics [/h1]

Northern Regime has a lot of its core systems implemented and ready to be added to and refined. A few of these systems include; crafting, animal breeding, animal migration, experience, weapons, level bonuses, reputation, and a few more. The game right now is getting really close to being a fully playable and fun experience. It takes a while to create a game that can be played for hundreds of hours, and it's especially hard to make a game fun. I think we are getting really close to accomplishing that feeling, but it will take many more hours to get it perfect. 

[h1] Kickstarter [/h1]

I'm not sure if we will make our funding goal with-in the next 20 days but it's okay. Kickstarter would have allowed us to take a little longer and really polish Northern Regime. This just means we will be able to get help from the community earlier in development. Something super amazing happened, though; Kickstarter gave our page a "Project We Love" badge and that really means a lot knowing that the staff at Kickstarter has an interest in our game and ideas. 

[h1] Road Map [/h1]

We're going to be working on a lot of pretty "minor" stuff. It's minor but in a sense, it makes the game. I'm talking mostly about adding different items, resources, plants, ores, etc. As well adding different crafting recipes and item unlocks. I usually procrastinate on adding new items because it's a little more intense than I would have imagined. It's not difficult to do but it requires so much art and models it's insane. To craft one item we have to make at least 4 models and 4 images. 5 items would be about 20 models or more depending on the recipes. When Northern Regime does come out we'll allow people to submit item ideas as well as the recipes. The next few months of development will pretty much consist of adding items, recipes, level unlocks, enemies, just small things that make the game feel like it has a large amount of content. 

[h1] Graphics [/h1]

A lot of development has been focused on quality and graphics. I have a heavy compulsion when Northern Regime doesn't look fantastic, so I am usually always tweaking the graphics and color scheme to try and accomplish the best look possible. I think now I am finally happy with how it looks so the graphics will most likely be untouched for the next little while to focus on making NR fun and engaging. I mean, most of the development for the next few months will be tweaking and polishing. 

[h1] Testing Team [/h1]

Developing a game for 12-14 hours a day you really start to forget about small bugs and problems. To get around this I would like to assemble a devoted team to test and report all bugs and problems they encounter. There will be a private forum on the Northern Regime website so the team can make entries. This will really help development form around the opinions of others which is what I really want to an extent. 

[h1] Release Date [/h1]

I personally would like to release sometime in November or even better, December. However, these are two months would be the worst time to release an indie title. Because it is near Christmas time, so many big companies release their games. I know we are not competing with these companies but we are competing to gain the same consumers which causes a conflict of interest. 

[h1] Outro [/h1]

I know this update wasn't totally about game-play, sorry for that. We will make sure the next update will go over Northern Regime a lot more, it will also come a lot sooner for you guys! Thanks for the support everyone, developing Northern Regime has been a total dream. I haven't enjoyed making anything more.

notes.title: Pre-Alpha 2.0.6
notes.content:
[h1] Introduction [/h1]

Hey everyone. We actually waited two weeks(2 Days early lol) to release an update, we're pretty proud of that. It's sometimes difficult not to release an update whenever, because we love sharing our progress and getting feedback from you guys. Development progress from these last two weeks is not as substantial as the few previous ones as our game engine has been crashing constantly, as well, it has just been extremely slow. 

[h1] Dynamic Artificial Intelligence [/h1]

Dynamic Artificial Intelligence is in it's very early stage, we just started working on it about one day ago. We thought we would include it to get some feedback on the concept. Although there isn't a lot to it, it's still quite interesting. Northern Regime will include a variety of different soldier camps posted along the landscape. Camps will either be; friendly, neutral, or hostile. When approaching a hostile camp they will shoot on sight with no questions asked. Coming across a neutral camp will be slightly different, If your weapons are holstered they will not engage in combat. You're free to walk around and explore their camp at your own will however, if you do pull out a weapon, accidentally or on purpose they will attack right away. We will be sure to expand on the different scenarios and approaches the player may take. For instance, you may pick up one of their items from the ground causing them to draw on you. The idea of maybe jailing the player depending on what he/she did or how he/she acted is in the air. The third camp is friendly, no matter what you do they will not attack based on their loyalty to you or your faction, however, attack friendly and even neutral soldiers will decrease your reputation substantially. 

[h1] Reputation & Role Playing [/h1]

It's been decided to bring back reputation and how apparent it will be in Northern Regime. Reputation and Role Playing are going to play a very large part in the players experience. We already touched on this in the section above, basically how your reputation decreases, but we are going to open it up and get in depth. If your reputation is absolutely terrible even friendly factions will be inclined to attack you. Camps and various soldiers will not be the only groups that reputation effects, Northern Regime is also going to involve; Traders, travelers, bounty soldiers, lost citizen's, homeless soldiers, and a few more as we progress. None of these groups will attack you, especially if your reputation is good, even if your reputation is extremely bad as they will fear you even more, however, there is the perk of them having the random chance of giving you items if your reputation is higher than normal. When approaching a random traveler or any character described above, having poor reputation they of course will not attack you, they will act kind and offer various items they have, seaming as if they like you but inside they are more fearful than anything else. These AI groups will dynamically wait for a good chance to attack you, whether it's when you holster a weapon or turn your back. Everything you do in the world will substantially effect your game play. The more evil of a character you are the harder it's going to be to actually play Northern Regime comfortably.  Of course you will always have the option to increase reputation based on different tasks you take and items you give to those who need them the most. Even hostile factions can be turned to neutral and maybe even friendly.

[h1] Real World Location [/h1]

It's pretty tough to design a large open world game, talking about time consumption and also even realism. I've never been the best at designing realistic landscapes and areas in games, to fix this major issue we decided to take data from a real world location in Northern Dakota(Where NR Takes Place) we took that data and inserted it into our game engine and actually created a world from it. This means Northern Regime actually takes place in a real world location. Not only is this much, much faster, it's also way more realistic. It's quite interesting too, I find myself just wandering around the map for hours exploring unique locations and different landscapes. I feel like I am actually walking through beautiful North Dakota. I hope players will really enjoy this and get immersed in it's uniqueness. 

[h1] Procedural Texturing [/h1] 

Another thing that has helped us a ton is procedural texturing. just like building a real world, texturing would take months especially to get a realistic feel and once again something I am not really good at. This procedural texturing is not completely random, it's more so based on the height of the terrain. The higher you go, the more rock and snow you'll experience. the lower in altitude you travel you'll see increased grass and decreased snow. It's never going to totally feel realistic but it's definitely a step in the right direction. 

[h1] Procedural Objects [/h1]

The world as it stands right now is about 60 kilometers in radius, and around 40 miles total. This creates a somewhat large complication. Placing loot, enemies, camps, etc. would take a very, very long time, time that could be spent in a more important function. A solid compromise would be to randomly and procedurally generate all of the enemies and objects. This may make it feel a little more realistic and definitely more unique to each player. However, procedural generation is really complicated and takes a lot of brain power. We already have a solid idea on how to do it. It's not going to be entirely random or totally procedural just to make it a little easier on us. We have already started on this generating pretty smalls objects like guns, coffee, and water cantines. This is actually fairly easy so I'm sure created other objects won't be the most difficult thing in the world. The worst outcome will be bugs like objects glitching in the ground causing frustration. We are going to make sure it works properly before we release. 

[h1] Animals, Nature, And The Ecosystem. [/h1]

Something we feel like will really make Northern Regime a different and unique survival game is how everything in the world is connected. We don't want to create a generic survival game because let's be honest, there are way too many out there. I'm not trying to slander survival games because I really do enjoy them I just think we all need something else on the table. I am going to use some information in a response I made to someone who started a discussion on this subject. Animals will be quite dynamic in a few senses. Regular gun fire will be a cause to deter animals from your area. The more gunfire in a particular area will cause serious migration. If you are a trigger friendly player odds are you will struggle to find animals to hunt. Another dynamic is excessive hunting, increased hunting in a location will cause other breeds to avoid those areas and take paths else where. Not only does this decrease your chance of finding animals to hunt it will also decrease the population and the likelihood of animals breeding. So Here's another dynamic : Having too many animals in your area will actually cause a decreased amount of plants and plant like resources. There's a plant in Northern Regime that is used to heal and replenish hunger, by adding it to boiled water then drinking. Deer and Moose are actually very likely to eat this, which may cause you to die. The more plant you yield will cause the animals of the area to have less food leading to starvation and death. It may sound extremely hard but really it's not that bad it just adds something strategy inducing into the game-play. Everything you do will directly effect the ecosystem. 

[h1] Summary [/h1]

Two weeks is a pretty long time to wait for an update, the reason why there is so much to touch on. We may have missed quite a few things but will be sure to include them into the next update. We hope you guys enjoy what has been added. If you want more constant updates you can follow our blog. If you want to check it out, it covers a lot of what I just talked bout with images and videos. Thank you everyone! 

http://www.northernregime.com/aga-blog

notes.title: Pre-Alpha 2.0.5
notes.content:
[h1] Introduction	[/h1]
    Hey everyone. We have decided to start releasing update notes every two weeks now. We were posting quite randomly and possibly too much, we are going to slow it down so we don't annoy everyone. If you do want to see constant updates you can follow our [url=https://twitter.com/AxelAnderson198] Twitter [/url] Or you can follow our [url=http://www.northernregime.com/aga-blog] Blog	[/url] Now that, that has been said, let's get into some notes and updates.

[h1] Name Change [/h1]
"Northern Regime" has officially been changed to "Northern Regime : 1862" The decision was made to stop some confusion revolving around the actually era  and timeline that the Northern Regime takes place. 

[h1] Open World [/h1]
The very first build of Northern Regime was an open world game that was cool and interesting however, it was confusing, a little dry, and it was not as fun as it could, or should have been. We are taking a whole new approach to the open world style. Not only will this be fun and captivating, if done right,  it will also be unique and different. This is a huge concern and I am sure it is to all of the followers of Northern Regime. There are so many open world survival games out there, all usually taking on the same theme that I think it really has deterred the average gamer from this genre. 

[h1] Voice Actor / Story Mode [/h1]
This is one big idea that will hopefully separate us from other survival open world games. We have hired a voice actor to give the character, you control, more life to make him feel less like a 3 dimensional model and more like someone you enjoy being around. When you explore this beautiful land your character will comment naturally on the different things you stumble upon. If you stumble upon a valley he'll tell you what he feels, if you see a camp raided by Native Americans he'll express his emotions, if you kill a deer he may feel remorse and some guilt. We are going to try our best to make this feel natural and beautiful in a sense. When exploring open worlds it's easy to feel lonely even if it is just a video game, this will help make it feel like you have a companion in your journey. 

We are going to hire a writer to create a story that goes along side history with a little fiction to spice it up. The hardest part will be making it dynamic and 360 degrees. Since the wold is open world we need to be able to tell a story at any area. What I mean by this is the story should be just as enticing and exciting even if you started it from the end, middle, or start and we already have a good plan/outline for it.

[h1] Hunting [/h1]
Hunting is going really well. It surprising how much immersion it can actually ad to the player experience. Currently the only animal present is a large male deer. It wanders, eats, and can hear you walking. Most are very timid and afraid, making hunting challenges in many aspects. You can kill the deer but right now it just gives you the meat as soon as it is dead. We'll be changing this to a cool skinning function. You'll get the meat and the fur to keep you warm. Stock piling meat will not be a great idea, the meat will go bad based on dynamic timing and the temperature.

[h1] Dynamic Breeding[/h1]
When you spawn in your first game there will be a random start number of all animals. When you refresh the game this will not be changed. The number of animals you get in the start is what you get...except, all animals will have dynamic breeding. [h1] Name Change [/h1]
"Northern Regime" has officially been changed to "Northern Regime : 1862" The decision was made to stop some confusion revolving around the actually era  and timeline that the Northern Regime takes place.

notes.title: What Direction Should Northern Regime Go In?
notes.content:
[u][h1] Hey guys. We've made a poll because we are looking for your input! [/h1][/u]



[b] Recently we've come up with a pretty major idea, that would of course majorly change the style of Northern Regime. Instead of a game play style most resembling Mount and Blade, but in a Civil War era, we have been thinking of changing the style to a more open world, adventure, crafting, and building type genre that we originally envisioned.

[u][h1] What Would Changing The Style Give Us? [/h1][/u]

[h1] Random Events [/h1]

[b]Snow blizzards[/b]

These would force the player to hide away in his tent, cave, house, fortress etc. These blizzards would cause major damage and would prompt Reconstruction, and re-fortification. 

[b] Native Indian Attacks & Confederate Attacks[/b]

Most common at night there would be a possibility based on the players vulnerability natives could attack your place of resting. You would need to hire trained guards to protect your camp when you are away or sleeping. The chance of failure of protection would depend entirely on the amount of guards you have and their corresponding level, as well as weapons. If failure did occur a portion of your supplies and resources would be taken. 

[h1] Building And Scavenging [/h1]

[b] Building Bases [/b]

You would be able to construct bases essentially anywhere you'd like. These bases could just simply be a tent and a camp fire to protect your self from the harsh weather of Dakota. This would leave you very vulnerable to random attacks. To build these bases you would need to either hunt for materials and chop down trees for wood or you could earn money by attacking other camps, stealing their supplies and selling them to other Indian Tribes or Union camps. 

[b] Scavenging [/b]

Scavenging would include already looted or villages, groups, tribes, and factions. Again scavenging would also include basic resource gathering, like hunting, mining, and chopping down trees. The nice thing about this, is it's all up to the player whether he/she would like to mine, hunt, or steal the supplies they need.

[h1] Friendships and Factions [/h1]

[b] Friendships [/b] 

Friendships would depend on how you carry yourself as a player. When starting a new game you would randomly become neutral, enemies, and friends with certain factions, tribes, and groups. Killing and attacking groups would diminish your friendships and create a more hostile environment. Helping friendly or enemy groups in war would increase likeliness with the group you chose to help and diminish friendship with the opposing group. The more liked you are by a group would increase the chance of them helping you with supplies, soldiers, and reinforcements. The more hated you are the more likely of attack and prejudice. 

[b] Charisma  & Other Attributes/Skills [/b]

Different attributes in the game would help you survive in the harsh war, and climate. Charisma as an example would help you create friendships with neutral and even enemy groups. 


[b] I don't want to go off all day and fill your feeds. I hope you get the point so far. Please vote to help us decide which you guys would rather enjoy playing as we said before, we really would like to be a community development group and build what you would like to see most..[/b]

[h1]Northern Regime Pre-Alpha 1.0.02. [/h1]
[b]
Subjects that will be covered in the following text :

New Map Selector.

[h1]Difficulty Of Game-Play[/h1]

	We have decided to increase the difficulty of game play for Northern Regime. When we first started developing and  working on Northern Regime the character felt to be more like a bullet sponge than a real person. By increasing difficulty we feel it adds more realism and makes combat more skill based. It is not as much fun if you can just run through a faction group guns blazing, complete the area in 30 seconds, and not have to even think twice about hiding to bandage your  character.
	 I'll explain how we are increasing the difficulty in a dynamic way. Getting shot by an enemy 3-4 times in a row, without healing will kill you almost instantly. This will force you as the player to slow down and take it easy from afar. This creates an interesting long range combat system. We increased bullet damage by almost two times what it was originally for the enemy  but, we have programmed a new enemy gun shot system. This system currently decreases accuracy the more your character moves as if the enemy is adjusting his sighting. So if you are remain frozen trying to aim down an enemy there is a bigger chance you will be killed. currently we are working on a new cover system. When you get near a wall you will be able to automatically lock to it to avoid being
 hit. 

[h1]Animations.[/h1]

This is just a short blurb. The previous update we talked about how we added a more dynamic character controller. With this we have
finally added additional animations, like backing up and crouching. 


[h1]Weapons Aiming.[/h1]

We have been working hard on programming a better aiming system with the new implementation of first person ADS. It right now is looking and feeling a lot better. When your character is not aiming down sights your cross hair will be quite large, aiming it  will then become about 3/4s of the original size, when you are crouching and aiming down sights it will be half of what it is normally. 

[h1]Looting.[/h1]

Northern Regime has a brand new randomly generated looting system, we also programmed a super easy loot editor so when ever we do want to create new awesome items for you guys it'll just take an image and then a few clicks of the mouse to add it. With this we'll be allowing the community to create unique items for the game. We'll have a community section on our website for people to submit their items or you can head over to our community hub - discussions to suggest  items right now. The new randomly generated loot system will take numbers from how many times you have been getting the same item it will then give you an increased chance of getting something in greater value. So if there is a bug, or if you have been getting super unlucky it will boost your chances to make you  happier. 

[h1]Patches.[/h1]

We fixed a major lag issue that has been stumping us for almost an entire month! You may have seen on our twitter we talked about how embarrassing it was. The explanation is basically we had our map selector choice algorithm on an endless loop. So the frame rate was still quite high but every few seconds while rotating you would receive a huge lag spike. This was just the script looping. We have fixed this and it gives us so much more motivation to continue working hard. 

[h1]Northern Regime Official EA Release Date.[/h1]

Given the response of our straw poll from the previous update we have decided to release on September the 29th. This will give us a tremendous opportunity to get criticism, ideas, opinions, and help from the community. To be able to receive this information it will give us so much perspective on what we need to be working on and what we need to add to make the community happy. Like we said  before we want this game to be molded by the people who play it. If you don't care about adding ideas, criticism, or  helping with development we suggest you wait to buy the game at a later date!

[h1]What to Expect.[/h1]

When we do release Northern Regime we hope to have at least 5-8 total groups to raid and one friendly group to buy and sell items from. The great 
thing about our new system is that you can revisit places on the map you have already defeated and fight again and gather more loot.So when we do add more content you will be prepared. We plan on releasing huge chunks of content; maps, items, new rares, new enemies, etc.every 2 weeks after early access is out to keep you guys happy and engaged. When Early Access is complete will will be releasing  dlc every single month and it will be as gigantic as we can get it. Dlc will be completely free for the entire lifespan of NR.

[h1]New Map Selector.[/h1]

Now when entering a group to raid you will be given a 2 dimensional map with the state of Dakota slit up into small sections to  choose from. As we progress through development the map will slowly expand until it is as big as it can get. 

[h1]Community Created Maps.[/h1]

We will be compiling a small bundle of our project into a pre-fab in which you guys can un wrap in your own unity project. This will include the base items and textures that we use to develop maps. This will allow you guys to develop your own cool maps that will be featured in the game if they are awesome enough :) Once again we will have a section on our website where you guys can submit these projects!

[h1] Minor Additions [/h1]
Added cross-hair. At long distances it was hard to tell if you had killed an 
enemy without proper confirmation. 

Worked on camera distance and movement for comfort.

Thank you everyone I look forward to hearing your thoughts!

notes.title: Pre-Alpha 1 Complete & Release Date
notes.content:
-[b] Alpha 1 [/b]

Northern Regime Alpha 1.0.0.0 is officially done. The map selection works well, the fighting and new animations are smooth, graphics have been improved, and lag has been changed substantially since the previous build. Northern Regime is now half third person and half first person. You will remain third person but when you aim in you will transform into a first person mode with your weapon drawn. This adds so much more immersion and excitement to battling those confederate enemies. 

-[b] New Character Controller[/b] 

We have also recently programmed a new movement and physics function to the game. Previously it was a little strange. We were strictly using a third person controller which didn't make sense when switching to first person mode. You couldn't run left of right without aiming in that direction. You also could not move backwards in any state. Another problem was physics and sliding, if you were to jump off a steep cliff or hill you would practically stay completely still. Now you will automatically slide down the hill not being able to stop yourself until you reach a flatter area. We plan to add a sliding animation in the near future. With the new controller we were also able to fix the movement speed of the character. The character now runs and walks at a realistic speed before it was slow and boring it may have been more realistic but it didn't feel right. We did try to change to speed by increasing animation speed but this made the game feel cheesy and even more unrealistic. With the new controller it will allow us to continue tweaking movement until we find a perfect medium. 

- [b]First Person Mode.[/b] 

First person was a little rough at the start as you might expect. When aiming in the enemies still felt very far away and almost invisible. This was do to our high field of view in the game. When aiming, now, your field of view will slowly decrease by 20 points from 80 making it feel as if you are adjusting your eyes, or closing one and leaving the other open, as you would if you were actually aiming down a sight. 

- [b]New Cross Hair. [/b]

Our old cross hair was merely a red cross lined to the center of your screen. 
This wasn't very optimal for the standards of Northern Regime. First of all it was red which really didn't fit the theme, it would have been okay if this was a low poly shooter. The new cross hair consists of 3 triangles making one triangle. One at the top and two at the bottom. The greatest thing about the new cross hair is if you are extremely far away it will be very difficult to hit an enemy. The old one was 100 percent accurate from really anywhere. We haven't added programming to the cross hairs yet, we plan to make it so when you do shoot they will expand for half a second or so then return smaller, we'll also add this to when you are running, rotating, and jumping we'll also need to make them even smaller when you are crouching and lying down. 


[b] Having A Good Time Exploring [/b]

Although Northern Regime will not be a complete Open World game, we still want to add exciting exploration and things to find in the maps you travel to. Instead of simple camps with a few tents and a few confederate enemies we are going to be adding awesome fortress' , buildings, traps, and all sorts of things to make the game a little more exciting and a little more lively. We have been testing out a few new fortress models with defense towers, and all we can say is we're glad we did so. When alpha 2 comes up we are going to be making new trailers and game-play videos to show off all that we had added so everyone can see what we have been doing! 

[b] Help From You Guys! [/b]

What would you guys like to see in the next update of Northern Regime? We are very open to ideas, opinions, and criticism from the community. So if you have anything to say to us we would love to listen! - Axel. 


[b]Release Date.[/b] 

We have set up a straw poll to get input on when you guys would like to see the game released and in what state you want it to be. It's very important to get feedback so please take a few seconds and vote! 
http://www.northernregime.com/northern-regime.html

[b] Thank You! [/b]

Before I head off, I would just like to thank everyone who has been supporting these posts with all the likes and feedback. It really makes a difference when making the game knowing there are people out there who want to play and follow along development. So thank you very much. I owe everything to the people following this awesome project!

Now you will automatically slide down the hill not being able to stop yourself until you reach a flatter area. We plan to add a sliding animation in the near future. With the new controller we were also able to fix the movement speed of the character. The character now runs and walks at a realistic speed before it was slow and boring it may have been more realistic but it didn't feel right. We did try to change to speed by increasing animation speed but this made the game feel cheesy and even more unrealistic. With the new controller it will allow us to continue tweaking movement until we find a perfect medium. 

- [b]First Person Mode.[/b] 

First person was a little rough at the start as you might expect. When aiming in the enemies still felt very far away and almost invisible. This was do to our high field of view in the game. When aiming, now, your field of view will slowly decrease by 20 points from 80 making it feel as if you are adjusting your eyes, or closing one and leaving the other open, as you would if you were actually aiming down a sight. 

- [b]New Cross Hair. [/b]

Our old cross hair was merely a red cross lined to the center of your screen. 
This wasn't very optimal for the standards of Northern Regime. First of all it was red which really didn't fit the theme, it would have been okay if this was a low poly shooter. The new cross hair consists of 3 triangles making one triangle. One at the top and two at the bottom. The greatest thing about the new cross hair is if you are extremely far away it will be very difficult to hit an enemy. The old one was 100 percent accurate from really anywhere. We haven't added programming to the cross hairs yet, we plan to make it so when you do shoot they will expand for half a second or so then return smaller, we'll also add this to when you are running, rotating, and jumping we'll also need to make them even smaller when you are crouching and lying down. 


[b] Having A Good Time Exploring [/b]

Although Northern Regime will not be a complete Open World game, we still want to add exciting exploration and things to find in the maps you travel to. Instead of simple camps with a few tents and a few confederate enemies we are going to be adding awesome fortress' , buildings, traps, and all sorts of things to make the game a little more exciting and a little more lively. We have been testing out a few new fortress models with defense towers, and all we can say is we're glad we did so. When alpha 2 comes up we are going to be making new trailers and game-play videos to show off all that we had added so everyone can see what we have been doing! 

[b] Help From You Guys! [/b]

What would you guys like to see in the next update of Northern Regime? We are very open to ideas, opinions, and criticism from the community. So if you have anything to say to us we would love to listen! - Axel. 


[b]Release Date.[/b] 

We have set up a straw poll to get input on when you guys would like to see the game released and in what state you want it to be. It's very important to get feedback so please take a few seconds and vote! 
http://www.northernregime.com/northern-regime.html

[b] Thank You! [/b]

Before I head off, I would just like to thank everyone who has been supporting these posts with all the likes and feedback. It really makes a difference when making the game knowing there are people out there who want to play and follow along development. So thank you very much. I owe everything to the people following this awesome project!

notes.title: Northern Regime Pre-Alpha 1.0.0.0
notes.content:
[h1] The First Build Of Northern Regime Alpha 1 Is Almost Complete. [/h1]

[b] Northern Regime Alpha 1.0.0.0 will be available on September 4th to those who have pre-ordered the basic package at http://www.northernregime.com/pre-order.html [/b]

[b] To See Images for this build http://www.northernregime.com/northern-regime.html[/b]


[h1] This Is What We Have Added To Alpha 1 [/h1]

Alpha 1.0.0.0 : 

[h1] Terrain Detail [/h1]

- Terrain has been improved drastically. It now uses bump maps to exude depth, previously seemed to appear as if it was painted on. this depleted in-game immersion. 

[h1] Format Change [/h1]

- Changed the layout of Northern Regime. It will no longer be an "Open World Game" It is still open world in a sense. Instead of walking around a large world it will now be split up into surfable map which allows you to instantly teleport to various camps. 

- Removed mines from Northern Regime. Resources will now be added by defeating groups, and then selling said resources to friendly faction branches located on the player map. 

[h1] Map Selector [/h1]

- Added a map selector. You can now surf through a large map to decide which groups and faction branches to initiate battles with. When you come close to a faction group a page will pop up in the center of your screen estimating the amount of possible members in the location, the yield you may receive from defeating the group, the location of where the group is, and the difficulty. These different hints will help you decide whether or not you are prepared to attack 

[h1] Quality Of Life [/h1]

- Added nice transitions and loading screens to make the game smoother and sleeker when loading the game or transitioning through scenes and menus.

- Lighting, shadows, and level detail have been improved immensely. 

- Character movement, speed, and animations have been improved to add realism and depth. Previously the character moved too slow, now that it is faster it does improve the excitement of battle and the game in general. 
 
- Fixed a major lag issue when rotating the character camera as well as preforming gun fights. The game now runs at 90-120 frames per second on a 
gtx 760, i5 3570k, and 16 gigabytes of run on windows 8. 

- Added more vibrant foliage, trees, sky, and ambient fog to increase liveliness of Northern Regime. 

- Added a dynamic day and night cycle. However, you most likely will not see an entire cycle as you won't be in a particular location for longer than 10-15 minutes at most depending on the group difficulty

[h1] Rag Dolls [/h1]

- Added rag doll physics to enemies. It was a bit repetitive to see the same boring animations preformed every time you killed an enemy. It makes the game more exciting and fun while capturing locations 

[h1] Combat Fix [/h1]

- Changed dynamics of combat. Damage on enemies can now take between 1-3 shots to kill, before it was a one shot kill each time which seemed unfair, and a little too easy. Enemies now do increased damage to the player depleting in between 19-29 damage each shot with slightly less accuracy. 

[h1] Resource Raiding [/h1]

- Added resource capturing. When defeating and enemy group you will be able to raid/capture their materials by pressing "E". A dynamic circle will appear  above the resources counting down from 5. Once it has counted down you will receive a group of random items and a random quantity of those items based on a randomly generated algorithm.
